newsitem.title: FRANCE: BNP says adjusts on UAP, 96 net unaffected.
newsitem.headline: BNP says adjusts on UAP, 96 net unaffected.

text.p: French bank BNP said on Wednesday that it would stop consolidating its UAP holding on December 31 and write the expected medium-term value of the shares' value into its accounts.
But it said asset sales would cover any gap and that its net result for 1996 would be unaffected and in line with the trend of the first half.
BNP bought into UAP at around 200 francs some time back and the reevaluation is expected to be for considerably less, around 157 francs, according to one estimate.

BNP said in its statement asset sales and formerly set aside provisions could be called on to cover the gap. BNP first-half net attributable profit was around 80 percent up on that of the previous first half at 1.735 billion francs.
The UAP changes follow the announcement last week that Axa and UAP were merging to create the second largest insurer in the world.
